content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/anchildress1/.claude/skills/pr-comment-review

Remediation workflow for an existing PR. Bot threads rot: unresolved thread, PR merges, the
"minor" finding was the real one. Every step below exists to close that gap.

GitHub MCP tools are preferred when loaded
(`ToolSearch("select:mcp__plugin_github_github__pull_request_read")`); `gh api` equivalents are
given inline.

## 1. Resolve the PR

Given a number/URL, use it. Otherwise:

```bash
gh pr view --json number,title,body,url,isDraft,baseRefName,headRefName
```

`owner`/`repo` come from whichever identified the PR. A supplied URL carries its own
`owner`/`repo` — parse them from it, because the PR may live in a repo the current checkout isn't
(same number, different repo, and every read and reply would land on a stranger's PR). Fall back
to `git remote -v` (origin) only for a bare number or the current-branch case.

No open PR for the branch → say so and stop. Don't guess.

## 2. Confirm both required bots reviewed

- Copilot: `copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]`
- Codex: `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`

```
pull_request_read(method="get_reviews" | "get_comments", owner, repo, pullNumber)
# gh api --paginate repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/reviews  |  .../issues/{pr}/comments
```

Read every page before concluding anyone is absent. `gh api` returns one page by default, so a
bot that reviewed after 30 other events looks missing without `--paginate`; the MCP tool pages
via `perPage` + the `after` cursor from `pageInfo`.

A missing bot is a diagnosis, not a shrug. Diagnose per bot — they have independent
configurations, so one explanation rarely covers both:

- **Draft PR** — check `isDraft`. This only explains Copilot if the repo has *not* enabled
  **Review draft pull requests** in its ruleset; with that on, a draft is no explanation at all
  and you need a different cause.
- **Pending** — last push minutes ago; report the timestamp instead of "absent".
- **No prior review history** — check whether the bot has ever commented on any PR here:

  ```bash
  gh api -X GET search/issues -f q="repo:{owner}/{repo} commenter:app/{bot-slug}" --jq '.total_count'
  ```

  `-X GET` is required — `-f` alone makes `gh` POST, and search answers with a bare `404` that
  reads like a missing repo. `{bot-slug}` is the login without the `[bot]` suffix.

  Report a `0` as **"no prior comments in this repo"** — never as "not installed". A freshly
  installed app, or one enabled before its first eligible PR, returns exactly the same `0`, and
  calling that an installation problem sends the user to fix something that isn't broken.

  There is no user-token API that answers "is this app installed"
  (`repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation` needs a GitHub App JWT and returns `401` to `gh auth`
  credentials). A recent review on *any* PR here is the practical proof — a bot that answered
  yesterday is installed today.

  You can also check whether this bot was requested, but **filter by who was requested** — a bare
  count of `review_requested` events counts requests aimed at humans and at the other bot:
  ```bash
  gh api --paginate repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{pr}/timeline \
    --jq '[.[] | select(.event=="review_requested")
           | .requested_reviewer.login // .requested_team.name] '
  ```
  Read the result carefully in both directions:

  - **Requested and silent**, while it answered other PRs in minutes → installed and
    not delivering. A bot-side failure, worth saying plainly.
  - **Never requested** proves nothing on its own. Bots that review automatically never appear
    here at all — Copilot shows up because a ruleset requests it, while Codex triggers on PR
    open / ready-for-review / an `@codex review` comment and so leaves no request event.

  Before declaring any automatic reviewer broken, **re-trigger it manually** and time the
  response. Posting `@codex review` is the supported path, and a bot that answers a manual
  trigger in minutes after missing the automatic one has a trigger problem, not an install
  problem — a much more useful thing to tell the user. Send them to **Settings → GitHub Apps**
  only when nothing else explains it.
- **Other** — state the evidence. Never "reason unclear"; if inconclusive, say what you checked
  and what came back, so the user doesn't re-derive it.

## 3. Drive every unresolved thread to a conclusion

```
pull_request_read(method="get_review_comments", owner, repo, pullNumber)
```

Returns `review_threads[]`, each with `is_resolved` / `is_outdated` / `is_collapsed` and its
comments — snake_case in the payload, even though the tool description spells them camelCase.
Page with `perPage` + `after` until `pageInfo.hasNextPage` is false; an unresolved thread on page
two counts exactly as much as one on page one.

The `gh api` fallback can't do this: REST `/pulls/{pr}/comments` returns flat comment records with
no thread resolution state. If you're on the fallback path, get it from GraphQL:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='query($o:String!,$r:String!,$n:Int!){repository(owner:$o,name:$r){
  pullRequest(number:$n){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{id isResolved isOutdated
  comments(first:100){nodes{databaseId author{login} path line body}}}}}}}' \
  -f o={owner} -f r={repo} -F n={pr}
```

Covers all sources — both bots, humans, SonarQube, Dependabot. For each unresolved thread:

1. Read the finding against the **current** code at that location, not the quoted hunk — code
   moves.
2. Fix or justify per §6.
3. Fixing → implement under the `code-implementation` skill's loop (research, implement, verify).
4. Reply **in that thread**. Never a top-level comment — not for a finding, not for a batch
   summary, not for a suppressed finding that carries no thread id. A standalone comment detaches
   the answer from the code it answers and is invisible to the thread's resolution state. Nothing
   is exempt. `commentId` is the numeric id from `#discussion_r<id>`, not the GraphQL node id:
   ```
   add_reply_to_pull_request_comment(owner, repo, pullNumber, commentId, body)
   # gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="..."
   ```
   A finding with no thread to reply to (Copilot's "suppressed comments", a review-body remark)
   gets a new review comment **at the relevant line**, which creates a thread. Never a bare comment.
5. State what changed, or exactly why nothing did. **Never cite a commit hash** — every force-push
   invalidates it, and a stacked-PR workflow force-pushes constantly, so the reference rots into a
   dead link that reads like evidence. Describe the change instead.
6. Fixed → **resolve the thread**. An answered-but-open thread is indistinguishable from an
   unanswered one at merge time, which is the rot this workflow exists to prevent.
   ```
   gh api graphql -f query='mutation($t:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$t}){thread{id isResolved}}}' -f t=<threadId>
   ```
   `threadId` is the GraphQL node id (`PRRT_…`) from the `reviewThreads` query, not the comment id.
   Leave unresolved only where nothing was fixed — a won't-fix or a finding awaiting the user's
   decision stays open as the visible marker that it is outstanding.

## 4. Check the PR's story against its diff

```
pull_request_read(method="get_diff" | "get_files", owner, repo, pullNumber)
```

Drift runs both ways: **undersold** (diff does things the body never mentions — drive-by fix,
dep bump, config change), **oversold** (body claims what the diff doesn't do, or describes a
superseded approach), **title scope mismatch** (title vs. what the diff actually touches).

Fix via `update_pull_request` / `gh pr edit`. Metadata correction — GitHub's edit history is the
trail, so no comment needed.

## 5. Self-review — once per PR, not per invocation

Only fixing what bots flagged outsources your judgment. But most invocations are a status check
or a follow-up on new comments, not the first pass.

Check for the marker `<!-- pr-comment-review:self-reviewed -->` in the PR's comments/reviews
first. Present → skip to §6 and say so ("self-review already done in <link>; say 'redo the
self-review' to force a fresh pass"). Run a fresh pass only if absent or explicitly requested.

Delegate the pass, scaled to risk:

- **Default**: `/code-review` at default effort — single pass, proportionate.
- **`high`+ only when warranted**: auth/security-sensitive code, unusually large diff, or the
  user asked for depth. Multi-agent review costs real time and tokens.

Findings follow §6. With no existing thread, post a review comment **at the relevant line** — a
line comment, which opens a thread; never a top-level one. Resolve it per §3 once fixed. Leave the
marker comment in place afterward.

## 6. No deferrals

**Every finding — either bot, human, or §5 — gets a fix or a specific, substantive reason it
won't be fixed. Neither is skippable.**

"Minor", "nitpick", "irrelevant", "follow-up" are not reasons; they're what gets written when no
decision was made. A real reason is independently verifiable by another engineer: touches an
unrelated module, needs a design decision only the user can make, depends on unlanded work,
would break an API this PR doesn't own.

A finding that needs a genuine tradeoff decision → stop and ask. Never invent a justification to
keep moving.

## 7. Verify, commit, report

Run the repo's verification loop (`make ai-checks` if present, else build + lint + test +
secretlint) before committing. Atomic commits, one logical fix each, matching recent `git log`
conventions.

**Do not push** unless this turn's invocation authorizes it. Default is commit and report "ready
to push".

```
## Reviewer presence
- Copilot: [present | absent — reason]
- Codex: [present | absent — reason]
- Other reviewers: [list | none]

## Threads addressed (N)
- [topic]: fixed — <what changed> — replied in thread, resolved
- [topic]: not fixed — <specific reason> — replied in thread, left open

## Title/description
- [accurate | corrected: <what changed>]

## Self-review
- [finding]: fixed — <what changed> — line comment posted, resolved
- [finding]: not fixed — <specific reason> — line comment posted, left open
(or "skipped — already done in <link>" | "none found")

## Needs your input
- [findings blocked on a human decision]

## Status
- N commits, [pushed | not pushed — say "push" to publish]
```

input.description: Fix pages.ts Codex findings
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker (SvelteKit 3, TypeScript strict, ESM, pnpm). Run every pnpm command with `VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1` set in the env.

Task: fix two real bugs reported by a code reviewer in src/lib/server/pages.ts (tests in src/lib/server/pages.test.ts). Do not touch any other source file.

Context: `fetchPage(url)` fetches a source page for a story. Internals: `guardedFetch` (manual redirects, max 3 hops, each hop SSRF-checked and DNS-pinned via an undici Agent), `readCapped` (reads body up to 2 MB), robots.txt check via robots-parser for UA "Gravespeaker". Keep the SSRF/DNS-pinning behavior exactly intact.

Bug 1: "If a source or its robots.txt sends headers but then stalls past the 8 s timeout or resets the connection, `reader.read()` in `readCapped` rejects outside any catch. The exception escapes `fetchPage`, so the snippet fallback in story.ts never runs and `Promise.all` rejects the whole fetch step." Fix: body-read failures must make that page unavailable (`fetchPage` returns null), never throw. For a failing robots.txt body read, treat robots as unavailable the same way a missing robots.txt is treated today (allow). Think about which is right and keep consistent with existing behavior for non-OK robots.txt.

Bug 2: "Robots permission is checked only for the original URL. When an allowed URL redirects to a disallowed path or another site's disallowed page, `guardedFetch(url)` follows redirects without consulting robots at the destination." Fix: apply the robots check for every redirect destination (same-origin or cross-origin) before fetching it. Suggested shape: give `guardedFetch` an optional per-hop `allowed(url: URL) => Promise<boolean>` callback that `fetchPage` supplies for the page request (fetching/parsing robots.txt for each hop's origin, reusing a small per-call cache keyed by origin so the same origin is not fetched twice); the robots.txt fetch itself should not recurse into robots checks. A disallowed hop makes the result null.

Add tests to src/lib/server/pages.test.ts (existing style: stub globalThis.fetch + mock node:dns/promises; behavior assertions, no "mock was called" assertions except where the existing DNS-pin test already does):
- body stream that errors mid-read -> `fetchPage` resolves null (does not throw)
- robots.txt body that errors mid-read -> page still fetched (allowed) and does not throw
- allowed URL redirecting to a path disallowed by robots.txt -> null
- allowed URL redirecting to another public host whose robots.txt disallows -> null
- redirect to an allowed destination -> text returned

input.description: Fix narrative sentence validation
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker (SvelteKit 3, TypeScript strict, ESM, pnpm). Run every pnpm command with `VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1` set in the env.

Task: fix a real grounding bug in src/lib/server/narrative.ts (`groundStory`), tests in src/lib/server/narrative.test.ts. Touch no other source file.

Reviewer finding (valid): "When the model supplies a real quote alongside an unsupported sentence, the check accepts the sentence as a documented fact without checking whether the quote supports it. Source text `Gaynor Hawks taught piano for forty years.`, quote `taught piano for forty years`, sentence `I flew combat missions in the war.` returns a `told` story containing the invented combat claim and its citation. Validate the factual sentence against the evidence before displaying it."

Today a `fact` sentence is kept if its sourceIds are all known and its normalized `quote` appears in a cited source's normalized text. The sentence TEXT itself is never compared with the quote.

Implement a deterministic check (no model calls) that a kept fact's `text` is supported by its `quote`. Product constraints (from the story prompt in src/lib/server/inference/gemma.ts, read it): fact sentences are delivered in a theatrical ghost voice, first person ("I taught piano for forty years", "I was preceded in death by my husband Arthur" from quote "preceded in death by her husband Arthur"). Flair is allowed; EXTRA CLAIMS ARE NOT. So pick a rule that rejects invented claims but tolerates pronoun/tense/filler changes. Recommended rule (adjust if you find something clearly better, and keep it simple, KISS/YAGNI):
- Normalize with the existing `norm`. Tokenize the sentence.
- Every number token and every capitalized word that is not sentence-initial in the original text must appear in the normalized quote, or be a token of the deceased's name (inscription.name, candidate.name, maiden name) or a month name.
- Of the sentence's remaining "content" words (length >= 4, not in a small English stopword/pronoun list you define as a constant), at least half must match a quote word, comparing by 4-character prefix so "teaching"/"taught"... style variants are not required to match but "preceded"/"preceded" are. A sentence with no content words fails.
Document the thresholds as named constants with a WHY comment. Facts that fail are dropped like other ungrounded facts (reconstruction sentences are untouched).

Tests (behavior, in the existing style): the reviewer's exact reproduction is dropped (write this test FIRST and see it fail before the fix); "I taught piano for forty years." from the quote "taught piano for forty years" survives; "I was preceded in death by my husband Arthur." survives given the source/quote "preceded in death by her husband Arthur"; a sentence adding a wrong number ("I taught piano for fifty years") is dropped; a sentence adding an unquoted proper noun ("I taught piano in Paris") is dropped; existing tests keep passing (adjust fixtures only if a fixture sentence was itself unsupported).

Rules: JSDoc on every function/method/class (eslint-plugin-jsdoc enforces it); inline comments only for WHY; no new dependencies; do NOT commit, push, or run `make ai-checks` / coverage (other agents edit other files in the same working tree). Keep file complexity low (Sonar S3776 limit 15 per function): extract small helpers.

Verify with: `VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1 pnpm exec vitest run src/lib/server/narrative.test.ts src/routes/api/story`, `VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1 pnpm exec eslint src/lib/server/narrative.ts src/lib/server/narrative.test.ts --max-warnings 0`, prettier --write on both.
Report: the rule as implemented (thresholds), tests added, exact results. No narration.

content.text:
The fact check is now strict enough to close the gap, and it's committed as `cd75781` (not pushed). `make ai-checks` passes with 113 tests.

## What changed
- **Claim words:** every claim word in a fact must come from its quote, in the quote's order, with number words equal to digits.
- **Negations:** a negation the quote doesn't contain is rejected.
- **Prompt:** the model is told to restate the quote's own words in the first person and put all flair in the imagined lines.
- **Tests added:** "famous pianist" and "never taught piano" are dropped. So are an invented "to the whole county" and a reordered sentence. "Arthur preceded me in death", a reversal of the quote, is dropped too.

## Live check
Two story runs came back "told" with real, quote-faithful facts (born date, piano for forty years, preceded by husband Arthur, the large garden). A third run failed with a lookup-service error, probably free-tier rate limiting after my repeated test calls; I didn't confirm.

## Limits
It still compares wording, not meaning. A fact that reuses the quote's words in order but swaps a single word could pass. The note's stricter option, showing the quote beside each fact, remains available if you want a guarantee. I left it out because it changes the UI.

## Your other questions
- **Approving your own PR:** you can't, so the Entire "Approvals" gate can't pass on your own account. That's a policy question for that tool, not something I can fix in code.
- **Flaky `robots.txt` sites:** I have no evidence of any. Nine of ten common record sites answered 200 in about 0.1–0.3 s. tributearchive.com answered 403, which counts as no rules. Fail-closed only triggers on 5xx, timeouts or broken bodies.

result.output:
The page covers Gemma 1, 2, and 3 formatting. It doesn't describe Gemma 4 formatting, though its navigation links to a separate Gemma 4 prompt-formatting page. The page also says it is deprecated and points to gemma.ai.

**System instructions**

- "Gemma's instruction-tuned models are designed to work with only two roles: `user` and `model`."
- "Therefore, the `system` role or a system turn is not supported."
- "Instead of using a separate system role, provide system-level instructions directly within the initial user prompt."

In other words, system-level guidance goes at the start of the first user turn.

**Control tokens**

The page lists `user`, `model`, `<start_of_turn>`, and `<end_of_turn>`. It describes `<end_of_turn>` followed by a newline as the turn separator. It also says the prompt prefix for the model's reply is `<start_of_turn>model` followed by a newline.

**Recommended prompt structure**

```
<start_of_turn>user
[system-level instructions, then the actual question]<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
```

The page's example puts a style instruction ahead of the question in the user turn, then leaves the model turn open for the reply.

**Multi-turn**

Turns alternate between `user` and `model`, each closed with `<end_of_turn>`.

**Custom fine-tuning**

The page notes that if you fine-tune a pretrained Gemma model on your own data, you can use any control-token schema, as long as it is consistent between training and inference.

input.prompt: What do the docs say about audio tags / stage directions in square brackets, which models support them (Eleven v3 vs Multilingual v2 / Flash), what happens to bracketed text on models that do not support them, and punctuation/prose guidance for natural narration?

result.output:
**Audio tags:** Bracketed tags such as `[whispers]`, `[laughs]`, `[sighs]`, and `[applause]` direct vocal delivery and sound effects. The docs describe them as a way to "direct delivery with fine-grained control." They're covered in the Eleven v4 section, which says its prompting techniques "also apply to Eleven v3," including audio tags.

**Model support:** The docs explicitly cover audio tags for Eleven v4 and Eleven v3. They don't say whether Multilingual v2 or Flash support audio tags. Those models appear only in the normalization and pronunciation sections. Phoneme tags work only with `eleven_flash_v2`, and alias tags are suggested for Multilingual v2, which doesn't support phoneme tags.

**Bracketed text on unsupported models:** The docs don't say what happens to bracketed text on models without audio tag support. The only related guidance is that Eleven v4 and v3 don't support SSML `<break>` tags, so you should use audio tags, ellipses, and text structure for pauses instead. Test bracketed text on any non-v3/v4 model before relying on it.

**Punctuation and prose for natural narration:**
- Ellipses add pauses and weight, and capitalization adds emphasis.
- Standard punctuation sets the rhythm of speech.
- Text structure strongly influences v4 output, so clear emotional context and natural phrasing help.
- Explicit dialogue tags give more predictable emotion than context alone, though the model may speak guidance text aloud. You can remove it in post-production.
- Writing in a narrative, scriptwriting-like style guides tone and pacing.
- Pace is also shaped by the voice's source audio. The speed setting ranges from 0.7 to 1.2, with 1.0 as the default.

**System role**
- Gemma 4 has built-in system-role support, which the page says enables "more structured and controllable conversations."

**Sampling parameters**
- The page recommends "Use the following standardized sampling configuration across all use cases": temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64.

**Thinking mode**
- Thinking turns on when the `<|think|>` token is at the start of the system prompt. Removing the token turns it off.

**Multi-turn conversations**
- Past model turns should keep only the final response, with tool-call turns as the exception where thinking is preserved.

**Multimodal prompts**
- Place image content before the text, and audio content after it.
- Image token budgets are 70, 140, 280, 560, or 1120. Lower budgets suit captioning and video; higher budgets suit OCR and document parsing.

**Audio prompts**
- The page provides templates for speech recognition and speech translation. The recognition template asks for digits rather than spelled-out numbers.

input.prompt: Summarize the recommended prompt structure for Gemma 4: system turn usage, what to put in system vs user turn, and any style guidance for instructions. Quote key rules.

result.output:
**Gemma 4 prompt structure**

**System turn**
- Open with `<|turn>system` and close with `<turn|>`.
- Put the thinking toggle here. Including `<|think|>` turns thinking mode on.
- Keep all system-level material in one system turn. The page says thinking mode "should be consolidated into a single system turn alongside your other system instructions", including tool definitions. Tool declarations use `<|tool>` and `<tool|>` in this turn.

**User turn**
- Open with `<|turn>user` and close with `<turn|>`.
- Place the user's request here, along with multimodal placeholders such as `<|image|>` and `<|audio|>`.
- The audio examples put their task instructions in the user turn.

**Model turn**
- Begin with `<|turn>model`. When thinking is on, the reasoning appears in a `<|channel>thought` block closed by `<channel|>`, followed by the answer.
- Between standard turns, strip the previous turn's thoughts before resending history. Keep thoughts between function calls within the same turn.
- For larger models without thinking, the page suggests an empty thought channel (`<|channel>thought` followed by `<channel|>`). It also recommends this for fine-tuning on data without thinking.

**Style guidance for instructions**
- The page says the model has "exceptionally strong instruction-following capabilities," so explicit directives work well.
- For audio tasks, it recommends structured instructions with bulleted format rules. For example, one rule reads "Only output the transcription, with no newlines."
- For thinking depth, you can add a system instruction asking for lower-depth reasoning, which the page calls a "LOW" thinking instruction. The page reports about a 20% reduction in thinking tokens. It presents this as a starting point to customize, not a fixed prompt.

The page does not give general style rules for everyday instructions beyond these examples.

Story (research R8, data-model Story/StorySentence, contracts/api.md /api/story response, spec user story 3 + FR-014/015/016 + Story entity + SC-004, quickstart manual step 4 and the narrative unit-test row): the story is now TWO model calls. If no verified fact says anything beyond the name, months and dates, the response is `{ status: 'insufficient' }` and the second call is skipped. (b) Prose, Gemma's recommended sampling (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64): the model writes ONE theatrical first-person paragraph (about 100-170 words, plain spoken prose, no stage directions or markup because it will later be read aloud by a voice service) from the verified fact quotes only. Current behavior to document:
1. Search (research R5): ONE integration, SerpApi, but several engines queried in parallel with plain fetch: google, bing, yahoo, duckduckgo, yandex (they all return organic results as link/title/snippet). Results are merged in that engine order and deduplicated by canonical URL (scheme, "www.", trailing slash, query and hash ignored; one Find a Grave memorial under any locale subdomain or slug is one page). One engine failing is tolerated; only losing every engine is a provider failure (502). Cost: one SerpApi search credit per engine per research request (5 credits).
2. Matching (R7) is a DETERMINISTIC engine in `resolveMatches(inscription, records)`; NO model call in research any more. Keys: name, birth year, death year. Name key = the surname (or the maiden name) as a whole word, accents folded, generational suffixes ignored, plus at least one of the stone's given names, in the title/snippet. Birth/death years are read from the text near the name, by label ("born", "died", "d.", "passed away"), by a range like (1932-2017), or derived from "age N" with a one-year slack; a `?` digit in the stone's year matches any digit. A key the result does not state is NEUTRAL; a stated year that disagrees EXCLUDES the result (a namesake). A result with the name and at least one matching date is kept even when its other date is missing. If no result confirms a date, name-only results are kept as UNVERIFIED (confidence low). When any result confirms at least one date, name-only results are dropped. Results are ordered by number of matching keys then by whether the page looks like a record (obituary, cemetery, grave, memorial, funeral, died, born); at most 5 become the candidate's sources. Output is zero or one Candidate. Confidence: high when every key the stone offers matches (and at least two), medium for two or more matching keys otherwise, low for name only. Candidate has no `place` field any more (removed), name = the inscription name, born/died = the year a matched result states or null. The confirm screen shows the confidence; low is labelled "Unverified: only the name matches. Check the sources before confirming."

A namesake whose snippet states no dates can still be returned, but only as unverified low confidence when nothing stronger exists, and the visitor must confirm with the sources visible. FR-009 should say the system must only attach records that match on name and do not conflict on a stated date, must label name-only matches as unverified, and the visitor always confirms.

Tests (quickstart, tasks): identity engine scenarios = right person with death date missing returned (medium); name plus both years high; age-derived birth; conflicting year excluded; namesake excluded while the real match is kept; different given name excluded; whole-word surname; maiden name; suffix; accents; `?` wildcard; name-only low; record-like ranking; far-away years ignored; cap 5 sources. ## What

The full MVP journey (spec `001-mvp-journey`): photograph a headstone, confirm who it is, hear a theatrical first-person story built from cited public records.

## How it works

- **Read:** Gemma 4 26B (via Mastra) reads the name and life dates. Code normalizes the output: honorifics, `née` split into a maiden-name signal, `?` for worn digits, letterless names dropped. A surname carved once on a shared stone applies to both people.
- **Research:** SerpApi is the only integration, but it runs Google, Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo and Yandex in parallel and dedupes by URL. A deterministic engine, with no model call, scores each result on name, birth year and death year. A missing date is neutral, a stated year that disagrees excludes the result, and a name plus one matching date is returned. Name-only results are kept as "unverified". Results whose stated dates contradict each other become separate candidates, so two people are never merged. Each candidate carries a high, medium or low confidence.
- **Story:** two model calls. First, facts are extracted as verbatim quotes at temperature 0, and code keeps only quotes found in the cited source and drops any that name survivors. Second, one theatrical paragraph is written from those facts at Gemma's recommended sampling. Code drops sentences that add a number, a name or a negation the facts do not give. The result is shown under "Story generated with AI" with its sources listed. No fact beyond the name and dates means the stone-only epitaph.
- **Page fetch guard:** public addresses only (including multicast, NAT64, 6to4 and Teredo blocks), DNS pinned to the checked address, redirects re-checked, `robots.txt` honored at every hop and treated as disallow-all when unreachable.

The search now uses three engines: Google, Yandex and Yahoo. The gate is green again (146 tests). Three commits are local, so nothing is pushed.

I committed `perf: search three engines instead of five…` before the gate had passed, which left one search test failing. The follow-up `fix: order the three engines by benchmark rank` repaired it, so the history has one broken commit in the middle.

## Which five
Google, Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo and Yandex, one credit each.

## Why these three
The ground-truth benchmark ran 10 stones against the real engines. It's saved as `benchmarks/results/search-1.json`, and records commit `2ecdb2b` and credits (201 before, 170 after, 31 used because SerpApi cached repeat queries).

| Engine | Results | Kept sources | Median time | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google | 91 | 22 | 60 ms (cached) | keep |
| Yandex | 58 | 9 | 2.1 s | keep |
| Yahoo | 17 | 3 | 4.0 s | keep |
| DuckDuckGo | 1 | 1 | 2.0 s | drop |
| Bing | 94 | **0** | **9.9 s** | drop |

Yahoo is the only engine that found matches for the common name (Gonzalez). A lookup is now 3 credits, and its wait is the slowest of three engines (about 4 s) instead of Bing's 10 s.

## Caveats
- **Small sample:** only 10 stones, and Google's time is flattered by the cache.
- **What it measures:** matches by my engine, not confirmed identity. Only 2 of 10 stones reached high confidence and 7 were low, because snippets rarely include dates.
- **Not yet run:** the end-to-end pipeline benchmark, which measures latency per stage, total time and read accuracy. It spends model quota plus 3 credits per stone. Do you want it on the same 10 stones?
- **To publish:** say "push" and I'll push these three commits.

The pipeline benchmark ran on all 21 fixtures. Results are in `benchmarks/results/pipeline-1.json` and committed locally as `1a6e319`. Four commits are unpushed.

## Results (commit `6e1dc94`, 3 engines)
| Stage | Result | Median time |
|---|---|---|
| Read | 63 of 64 fields correct (98%) | 5.5 s |
| Research | 17 of 20 found a candidate: 2 high, 0 medium, 15 low | 6.4 s |
| Story | 12 told, 4 insufficient evidence, 1 timeout | 11.6 s |
| Whole journey | 24.3 s per stone | |

The whole run took 768 s, of which 300 s was one timed-out story.

## Problems
- **Dixon timed out.** The story call hit the 300 s limit after research returned a low-confidence candidate. This is the one error, and I haven't found the cause. Gemma may have hung, or a page fetch may have stalled.
- **Low confidence dominates.** 15 of 17 candidates match on name only, because snippets rarely carry dates. The 4 "insufficient" stories come from the same cause: too little evidence.
- **No match for three stones:** Chambers, Hawks and Holmquist.
- **Illegible marble** was skipped correctly, with no research attempted.

## Open items
- I ran all 21 stones, not the 10 I proposed. SerpApi credits left should be about 110, assuming no cache hits.
- The PR #5 description still says five engines.
- To publish the four commits and update the description, say "push".
- To find the cause of the Dixon timeout, say so and I'll look into it.

input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker (SvelteKit/TS strict, ESM). Read CLAUDE.md first. You own ONLY src/lib/server/narrative.ts and src/lib/server/narrative.test.ts. Codex review finding (P2) to fix: "Recognize supported facts composed entirely of short words. If the only verified biographical fact uses words shorter than five characters, topicStems returns an empty set and groundParagraph's fact-use condition always excludes it, even when the paragraph repeats it exactly. Example: verified quote `was a chef` passes hasEvidence, but grounding `I was a chef.` returns insufficient. Add a matching fallback for facts without long topic words rather than treating them as unused."
Read narrative.ts (topicStems, STEM_LENGTH=5, MIN_FACT_USE=0.5, groundParagraph, hasEvidence) and fix it so a fact with no stems of STEM_LENGTH+ falls back to matching on its shorter content words (e.g. drop stopwords/very short function words, then require the same MIN_FACT_USE share), so `I was a chef.` is accepted as using that fact, while a paragraph that does not mention the fact still counts it unused. Add a regression test in narrative.test.ts that fails before the fix, plus a negative case (paragraph unrelated to the short fact → still insufficient). Keep every existing guard (numbers, mid-sentence proper nouns, negations, dedupe).

Rules: JSDoc (one-line summary, @param, @returns) on every function; inline comments explain WHY only; tests assert behavior, never exact prose of model-style output. input.description: Fix identity engine Sonar and Codex findings
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker (SvelteKit/TS strict, ESM). Read CLAUDE.md first. You own ONLY src/lib/server/identity.ts and src/lib/server/identity.test.ts. Other agents edit pages.ts, url.ts, narrative.ts: do not touch them. Do NOT commit, push, stage, or edit config files. identity.ts is the deterministic matching engine (resolveMatches: name key + birth year + death year, 2 of 3 keys, confidence high/medium/low, contradicting stated years become separate candidates). Read it and identity.test.ts fully before changing anything.

A. Sonar (fix in code, behavior unchanged): S7780 "String.raw should be used to avoid escaping \" on identity.ts lines ~7, 96 (x2), 123, 152, 157, 158; S6397 "Replace this character class by the character itself" at ~line 159. Convert the affected string-built RegExp sources to String.raw / drop the pointless class. Existing tests must still pass.

B. Four Codex review findings; each needs a fix AND a regression test that fails before the fix:
 1. P1 (~line 190) Name tokens must form ONE person's name: the surname and given-name checks are independent token searches, so "Charles Hawks (1932-2017). Survived by Gaynor Jones." matches Gaynor Claire Hawks (1932-2017) at high confidence (Gaynor from "Gaynor Jones", Hawks from "Charles Hawks"). Require the given name and the family name to be adjacent/in the same name phrase (allow middle names/initials, nickname, maiden name, "Surname, Given" ordering) so tokens from different people cannot combine, before nearby dates are used.
 2. P2 (~line 203) When the stone lacks birth/death dates, compareYear returns 'none' and the candidate's born/died come out null even though sources state them. Two records "Gaynor Hawks (1932-2017)" and "(1942-2020)" yield two separate candidates with born/died null. Preserve the source's stated years in the candidate's born/died regardless of whether the stone can confirm them (still never invent; use only years the source states, and keep the existing rule that a missing stone date is neutral for matching).
 3. P2 (~line 124) Dates in day-first ("10 March 1940") or numeric ("03/10/1940") form are missed, so "Gaynor Hawks, born 10 March 1940, died 2017." against a stone born 1932 is accepted instead of excluded ("born March 10, 1940" is excluded correctly). Recognize day-first and numeric (dd/mm/yyyy, mm/dd/yyyy, yyyy-mm-dd) formats where a year is stated, before the year-conflict check.
 4. P2 (~line 162) Age-derived birth year uses a symmetric slack (+-1), which accepts a birth year LATER than died-age. A stone born 1933, died 2017 with record "Gaynor Hawks, age 85, died December 27, 2017." returns high confidence, but age 85 in 2017 means born 1931 or 1932. Use the directional interval [died-age-1, died-age] for conflict checks and grouping.

Rules: JSDoc (one-line summary, @param, @returns) on every function incl. named arrows; inline comments explain WHY only; tests assert behavior with scenarios (records in, candidates/confidence out), never prose; keep regexes linear (Sonar S8786/S5852 are enforced). Keep the whole existing identity.test.ts passing. Run only: `pnpm vitest run src/lib/server/identity.test.ts src/routes/api/research`, `pnpm eslint src/lib/server/identity.ts src/lib/server/identity.test.ts --max-warnings 0`, `pnpm exec prettier --check` on those files. content.text:
The Depot CI run fails for two separate reasons. Neither comes from the code changes. I haven't fixed either one yet.

**1. `CI / ci` fails at the E2E step, with 3 of 15 mobile tests failing.**
- **Where it fails:** the unit tests pass (162), and the build, lint and type check pass. The 3 failures are `a failed story shows the message and retries`, `a non-JSON 413…` and `an unverified match…`. Each one uploads a photo and then waits for UI that never appears.
- **Why I think it's a load flake:** the same tests pass on my machine, and passed on GitHub's runner earlier. I reproduced it by running the suite under heavy CPU load. The failures were the same kind (`This is them` never found, `setInputFiles` timing out, alerts missing), but in different tests each run, plus one failure in an unloaded run. A deterministic bug would hit the same tests every time.
- **Likely mechanism, not proven:** the test's `upload()` helper picks a file right after `page.goto`. On a slow runner the page may not have hydrated yet, so the upload is ignored. I haven't isolated that as the cause.
- **Second problem:** `playwright.config.ts` matches `**/*.e2e.ts`, so it also runs the `.worktrees/all-hallows` copies of the tests. Locally that doubles the load. On CI there's no worktree, so it isn't the cause there.

**2. `CodeQL / Analyze` fails at the Initialize CodeQL step.**
- It gets `Not Found` from GitHub's workflow-runs API while checking its PR cache. Depot's runs aren't GitHub Actions runs, so there's no GitHub run for CodeQL to look up.
- The workflow already has `actions: read`, so granting that permission won't help. The likely fix is to turn off CodeQL's overlay cache for these runs. I'd need to check CodeQL's docs for the exact setting.

**Decisions for you:**
1. Should I fix the e2e flake by making `upload()` wait for hydration, and exclude `.worktrees` from Playwright? That second part edits `playwright.config.ts`, a repo config file. I'd verify the fix by repeating the suite under CPU load.
2. For CodeQL, should I find the overlay setting and edit `.depot/workflows/codeql.yml`, or leave CodeQL off Depot? I'd put CodeQL back on its GitHub workflow, which was passing.

I also stopped the CPU-burner processes I started for the load test.

exclude worktrees. make upload wait give me pros and cons. 
use depot cli to troubleshoot failing workflows

The search didn't turn up official documentation for a `CODEQL_ACTION_OVERLAY` variable that disables overlay analysis. The results point to a different mechanism, plus a few related details.

- **Repository property (most direct option):** Organizations can create a custom repository property named `github-codeql-disable-overlay`, then set it to true on a repo to turn off improved incremental analysis. First, create a custom repository property with the name github-codeql-disable-overlay and the type "True/false" in the organization's settings. Then in the repository's settings, set this property to true to disable improved incremental analysis. A changelog entry says this property also works on GitHub Enterprise Server. The CodeQL Action now loads custom repository properties on GitHub Enterprise Server, enabling the customization of features such as github-codeql-disable-overlay that was previously only available on GitHub.com.
- **Pull request behavior:** One changelog says improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run.
- **Environment variable:** A PR about overlay fallback says the disk-space fallback applies only when overlay analysis is enabled by feature flag and is ignored if overlay analysis is enabled by environment variable. That implies an env var can force overlay on, but I found nothing confirming a `CODEQL_ACTION_OVERLAY` variable that turns it off. Feature-flag env vars follow a pattern like "CODEQL_ACTION_OVERLAY_ANALYSIS_SWIFT", which suggests the naming convention but isn't proof.
- **Caveat on sources:** Most hits were dependency-bot notices, mirror sites, or PR pages, not the official docs. Check the codeql-action README and release notes before relying on any variable name. The changelog also mentions passing `trap-caching: false` to the init action as a workaround for one related change.

## Making `upload()` wait: options

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **A. `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` after `goto`** | One line, no app change. Our preview server has no long-lived connections, so it settles. | Playwright discourages it. It waits on timing, not on hydration itself. |
| **B. App sets a ready marker on mount, test waits for it** | Deterministic: it waits for the exact thing that failed. Works on any runner speed. | Adds test-only code to the app. |
| **C. Retry the upload until the next screen appears (`toPass`)** | No app change, and it tolerates slowness. | It also retries when the app is really broken, which hides bugs. Slower failures. |

My recommendation is **A**. It's the smallest diff, and the app stays free of test hooks. If it flakes again, move to B. Which one do you want?

#4403465359 src/lib/server/narrative.ts:70
Restrict number normalization to own dictionary entries**

If a verified quote or generated sentence contains `constructor`, this lookup returns the inherited `Object` constructor instead of the original word. `topicStems` then calls `.slice()` on that function and throws, failing the entire story request rather than returning a story or epitaph. A direct reproduction with the verified quote `worked as a constructor` and paragraph `I worked as a constructor.` throws `TypeError: canon(...).slice is not a function`. Use an own-property lookup, a null-prototype dictionary, or a `Map`, and apply the same restriction to the number-membership check in `sentenceHolds`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

#4403471727 src/lib/server/pages.ts:41
The SSRF deny-list still accepts IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals: `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is classified as IPv6, but none of the listed IPv6 ranges cover `::ffff:0:0/96`, so this URL can reach `fetchHop` instead of being rejected. The new `pages.test.ts` case for this address therefore does not match the implementation. Block the mapped range or normalize mapped addresses to IPv4 before applying the IPv4 rules.

#4403471809 src/lib/server/pages.ts:157
`guardedFetch` returns a malformed 3xx response when it has no `Location`, and this branch treats every non-OK response below 500 as allow-all. That means an unreadable `robots.txt` can bypass the required disallow-all fallback. Only 4xx should mean “no rules”; other non-2xx responses should be rejected.

#4403471878 src/lib/server/narrative.ts:47
This survivor filter recognizes only a few lead phrases. A common obituary quote such as “her husband John” can pass verification, and `John` is then in `quoteWords`, so the prose checker explicitly allows the model to repeat that survivor's name. Reject named-relative quotes unless a predeceased cue is present, or strip/drop those names before they reach the story, to uphold FR-017.

This issue also appears on line 181 of the same file.

#4403471933 src/lib/server/story.ts:15
The API contract documents candidate sources as 1–5, but this request schema only enforces a minimum. A direct caller can submit an unbounded source list; page fetching stops at five, while `extractFacts` still serializes every candidate source into the model prompt, allowing oversized requests and unnecessary provider cost. Enforce the documented maximum at this boundary.

#4403472004 specs/001-mvp-journey/research.md:40
This cost note is inconsistent with the implementation and the PR description: `ENGINES` contains only Google and Yandex, so each research request uses two SerpApi search calls/credits, not three. Please correct the documented quota estimate so the operational limit is not overstated.

#4404165040 src/lib/server/identity.ts:185
Stop date extraction at another life-event cue**

When a snippet gives a birthplace without a birth year, `[^.\d]{0,40}?` can consume the subsequent death cue and interpret the death year as the birth year. A direct reproduction with the stone born in 1932 and died in 2017 and the snippet `Gaynor Hawks, born in London, died in 2017.` returns no candidates, whereas the same snippet without `born in London,` correctly returns a medium-confidence match. Prevent the birth-year search from crossing a death cue so records with an unstated birth year remain neutral rather than being excluded as contradictory.

## What

The full MVP journey (spec `001-mvp-journey`): photograph a headstone, confirm who it is, hear a theatrical first-person story built from cited public records.

## How it works

- **Read:** Gemma 4 26B (via Mastra) reads the name and life dates. Code normalizes the output: honorifics, `née` split into a maiden-name signal, `?` for worn digits, letterless names dropped. A surname carved once on a shared stone applies to both people.
- **Research:** SerpApi is the only integration, but it runs Google and Yandex in parallel and dedupes by URL. A deterministic engine, with no model call, scores each result on name, birth year and death year. A missing date is neutral, a stated year that disagrees excludes the result, and a name plus one matching date is returned. Name-only results are kept as "unverified". Results whose stated dates contradict each other become separate candidates, so two people are never merged. Each candidate carries a high, medium or low confidence.
- **Story:** two model calls. First, facts are extracted as verbatim quotes at temperature 0, and code keeps only quotes found in the cited source and drops any that name survivors. Second, one theatrical paragraph is written from those facts at Gemma's recommended sampling. Code drops sentences that add a number, a name or a negation the facts do not give. The result is shown under "Story generated with AI" with its sources listed. No fact beyond the name and dates means the stone-only epitaph.
- **Page fetch guard:** public addresses only (including multicast, NAT64, 6to4 and Teredo blocks), DNS pinned to the checked address, redirects re-checked, `robots.txt` honored at every hop and treated as disallow-all when unreachable.

## Verification

- `make ai-checks` and `make e2e` pass: 146 unit tests, 15 Playwright tests on a 390 px viewport. Unit tests assert behavior, not prose.
- Benchmark run 11 (21 reviewed stones): 63/64 fields, 3.8 s median. Earlier runs are untouched. `benchmarks/search.ts` and `benchmarks/pipeline.ts` record search and end-to-end runs and save their output as they go.
- Semgrep and gitleaks clean. CodeQL passes. All Sonar issues from the first scan, every Copilot and Codex thread, and the Entire findings are addressed.
- Mobile Lighthouse on the preview build scored 100 on all four categories (before the latest UI changes).
- Walked through on a desktop and on a phone against the preview server.

## Notes for review

- **New dependencies:** `@mastra/core`, `zod`, `@mozilla/readability`, `linkedom`, `robots-parser`, `undici` (needed to pin DNS). The `serpapi` package was dropped because it uses `https` and can't be mocked at the network boundary.
- **SerpApi cost:** one search credit per engine, so two per lookup, on a Free Plan of 250 a month. Engines were chosen from `benchmarks/results/search-1.json` (10 stones). End-to-end timings and accuracy are in `benchmarks/results/pipeline-1.json`. SerpApi's status page also lists open Google and Bing quality and advanced-operator incidents; one failing engine is tolerated.
- **Spec changes:** FR-006 no longer searches by maiden name, and the story is one labelled paragraph instead of separated fact and imagined lines.
- **Accepted for the MVP:** `/api/story` trusts the candidate the browser sends. The later fix is a signed candidate or re-running research (research R9).
- **Fixtures:** the new `holmquist-2024.jpg` is kept out of this PR and stays local. The photo already exists in earlier history; this PR only adds its answer key.
- **Known limits:** the story check compares numbers, names and negations, not free-prose meaning. The deny-list is complete for special-use ranges but DNS is trusted once per hop.

#4404855789 PRRT_kwDOVZZb886xRr1R
Normalize compound numbers before comparing factual sentences**

When the model spells out a compound number that the source writes as digits, this token-by-token comparison drops a fully supported sentence. A direct reproduction with the verified quote `taught piano for 24 years` and paragraph `I taught piano for twenty-four years.` returns `insufficient`; the reverse conversion fails too. Consequently, an ordinary change in number formatting can replace a usable story with the insufficient-evidence epitaph. Normalize complete number expressions consistently in both quotes and sentences before checking membership.





#4404855800 PRRT_kwDOVZZb886xRr1d
Exclude age and ordinal date wording from substantive evidence**

When a source restates life dates using ordinary age or ordinal wording, this check mistakes the remaining tokens for additional biography. For the existing stone dated March 10, 1932–December 27, 2017, both `died December 27, 2017 at the age of 85 years` and `was born on March 10th, 1932` make `hasEvidence` return true, and matching paragraphs return `told`. Here `years` or `10th` is the only purported additional information, so `tellStep` unnecessarily generates an AI story instead of taking the required stone-only fallback. Recognize these date-only expressions without excluding genuine birthplace or other substantive information.





#4404907258 PRRT_kwDOVZZb886xRzcj
Retain given-name initials when matching identities**

When a stone gives only initials before the surname, this filter removes every given-name token, and `phraseStart` then accepts any occurrence of the surname without checking the initials. A direct reproduction with `J. Smith`, born `1932`, died `2017`, and the record `Mary Smith (1932–2017), a schoolteacher.` returns a high-confidence candidate backed by Mary's obituary. Preserve and compare the initials, or avoid treating the name as confirmed when no given-name evidence remains, so explicitly incompatible namesakes cannot reach the story flow as strong matches.

#4405725403
Remove enclosing punctuation with the maiden-name clause**

When the reader transcribes a parenthesized maiden name, such as `Gaynor Hawks (née Staples)`, normalization produces `name: "Gaynor Hawks ("` and `maidenName: "Staples)"`. The remaining parenthesis becomes the surname in `nameParts`, so `resolveMatches` rejects even a record explicitly naming `Gaynor Hawks (1932–2017)` with matching dates. Remove the complete parenthesized clause and keep punctuation out of the maiden-name signal so this valid inscription can reach identity confirmation.





#4405727945
Require whole-word boundaries when verifying source quotes**

When an extracted quote matches only part of a source word, `includes` still promotes it to a verified fact. A direct reproduction with source text `Gaynor Hawks remained unmarried.` and extracted quote `married` passes `verifyFacts`, and `groundParagraph` then returns a cited, `told` story saying `I married.` This reverses the source's meaning before sentence grounding even runs. Require the normalized quote to match complete source tokens, including boundaries at both ends.
